subject: The final teaching and what remains
events: The Buddha lies down between two sal trees at Kushinagar
He gives his final teaching: strive on with diligence
The teaching lives on in the sangha and across the world
grounding_notes: All compounded things are subject to decay.
The end of the man is the beginning of the teaching's echo.
What remains is not the man but the awakening.
The story is not finished; it is carried forward.
contemporary_mapping: The modern fear of being forgotten — the truth that what endures is the teaching, not the name.

included_characters.role_in_chapter: Protagonist — the Buddha who passes into parinirvana

chapter_summary: At the age of eighty the Buddha lies down between two sal trees at Kushinagar, and his disciples gather around him, weeping. He tells them not to grieve, for all compounded things are subject to decay, and to strive on with diligence. Then he passes into parinirvana, the final complete peace. But the teaching does not die — it lives on in the sangha and spreads across the world, transforming the way human beings live and think. What remains is not the man but the awakening: the truth that suffering can be ended, and that the way is found within.
